# Three canvas remotes have no callers left, and removal is an API break

## Context

PR #19045 replaces the inward canvas transfer with a document-local presenter: the Canvas Worker builds its own `OffscreenCanvas` and ships frames out, instead of adopting a canvas a document hands it. That makes the old path unreachable **from this repository** and leaves it exported.

This is the API half, deliberately split out. @neo-opus-vega's framing when accepting the decomposition: piece 4 is the API leaf, *"with `worker/Canvas.mjs:37` stated"* — the line that makes it an API question rather than a cleanup.

## The Problem

`git grep` on PR #19045's head finds **zero in-tree code callers** for any of these. The single `getOffscreenCanvas` hit is an archived tickets JSON under `apps/portal/resources/data/`, not code.

| surface | exported at | state |
|---|---|---|
| `main.DomAccess#transferCanvasToWorker` | `DomAccess.remote.app` | was the inward transfer entry; zero callers after #19045 |
| `main.DomAccess#getOffscreenCanvas` | `DomAccess.remote.app` | superseded by #9479; already had zero callers before #19045 |
| `worker.Canvas#retrieveCanvas` | **`worker/Canvas.mjs:37`**, `remote.app` | same generation; already had zero callers |

Three more are unreachable but **not** exported, so they are ordinary dead code and carry no deprecation question:

- `worker.Canvas#registerCanvasDirect` — reachable only from `transferCanvasToWorker`
- `worker.App#onCanvasRegistered` and the `registerCanvasCallbacks` bookkeeping it drives — #19045 deleted the component side that populated it
- `worker/Manager.mjs:183` routes `message:getOffscreenCanvas` to `DomAccess.onGetOffscreenCanvas`, **which is defined nowhere in the tree**. That route has been broken for longer than this work and nobody noticed, which is its own small argument for removing the family rather than leaving it.

**Why this is not just a delete.** `remote.app` is the App Worker's public surface. An application built on Neo — outside this repository, on its own release cadence — can call `Neo.main.DomAccess.transferCanvasToWorker(...)` today, and "no in-tree caller" says nothing about that. Removing an exported remote is a breaking change and needs the call made deliberately, not as tidy-up riding along in a feature PR.

## The Architectural Reality

- The presenter path added by #19045 does not use any of the three; it is additive and they are simply no longer reached.
- Leaving them exported keeps the failure #18376 is about **reachable by an external app**: `transferCanvasToWorker` still hands a document's canvas to a worker that may be hosted elsewhere. That is the argument for removal rather than indefinite tolerance, and it is why this should not sit open forever.
- `worker.Canvas#unregisterCanvas` stays either way. It is still exported, and #19045's `onReleasePresenterCanvas` deliberately did not change it — the two have different scopes (whole `nodeId` vs one window).

## The Fix

Decide, then do one of:

1. **Remove**, with a release note naming the replacement (`registerPresenter` / `unregisterPresenter`) and the version. Removes the last reachable route to the renderer kill.
2. **Deprecate for one release**, warning on call, and remove after. Costs a release of carrying a path that can still terminate a renderer.

Either way the three unexported leftovers go, and `worker/Manager.mjs:183`'s route to a non-existent handler goes with them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — The choice between removal and a deprecation window is recorded here with its reason, before any code moves.
- [ ] AC-2 — Under the chosen option, `git grep -n 'transferCanvasToWorker\|getOffscreenCanvas\|retrieveCanvas' -- src/` returns only what that option intends, and the PR body shows the output.
- [ ] AC-3 — `worker/Manager.mjs:183`'s route to the undefined `onGetOffscreenCanvas` is gone regardless of which option is chosen; it is broken today and belongs to no contract.
- [ ] AC-4 — `apps/portal` still boots with canvases painted — `test/playwright/e2e/core/PresenterTransport.spec.mjs` green at both DPR arms, which is the witness that removal took nothing live with it.
- [ ] AC-5 — If removal is chosen, the release note names the replacement API; if deprecation, the warning names it.

## Out of Scope

- The presenter contract itself — #18376's AC-2, delivered by PR #19045.
- `worker.Canvas#unregisterCanvas`. Still exported, still used, different scope from the per-window release.
- Any behaviour change to the presenter path. This ticket only removes what no longer runs.

## Decision Record impact

`none` for option 2; option 1 is a breaking change to a documented remote and wants a release note rather than an ADR.

## Related

- #18376 — the defect whose repair made these unreachable
- PR #19045 — the presenter transport; this is its promised follow-on

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-22T23:51:09Z

Closing — the premise is void. This ticket assumed PR #19045 had replaced the inward canvas transfer. #19045 closed unmerged, and #18376 is now closed into D#18730. On `dev` the transfer path is live: `component/Canvas.mjs:94` still calls `DomAccess.transferCanvasToWorker`, which reaches `worker.Canvas#registerCanvasDirect`.

What stays true, measured on `dev` today and independent of #19045, is carried to D#18730, because the successor's canvas-worker rework owns this family:
- `main.DomAccess#getOffscreenCanvas` — exported (`DomAccess.mjs:84`), defined (`:965`), no caller.
- `worker.Canvas#retrieveCanvas` — exported (`Canvas.mjs:37`), defined (`:178`), no caller.
- `worker/Manager.mjs:183` routes `message:getOffscreenCanvas` to `DomAccess.onGetOffscreenCanvas`, which is defined nowhere: a broken route.
